candidates.hook: Your GTM asset can be perfectly on-brand and still be strategically unauditable.
progression: Expose the decision debt hidden behind a polished final asset.
Separate approved evidence from the editorial inference introduced during production.
Place the unresolved release condition beside the named human owner.
Hand practitioners a five-field audit they can apply immediately.
body: OPERATING TENSION: The asset passes review, yet nobody can reconstruct which audience assumption survived, which evidence supported it, or who accepted the remaining uncertainty.
DECISION RULE: An asset is review-ready only when its source brief, approved fact, editorial inference, release owner, and unresolved condition remain inspectable together.
PROOF BOUNDARY: ProofLaunch Cortex-X is a governed multimodal GTM employee that binds approved evidence, generation, review, activation preparation, and learning without automatic external release.
PRACTITIONER ACTION: Take the last asset your team approved and label those five fields. The blank field is the next review question, not another prompt.
FAILS WHEN: A senior operator reads the record and still cannot explain why this asset, for this audience, deserves a human release decision.
candidates.cta: Inspect the evidence trail; consider the design-partner cohort only if it exposes a decision your current stack hides.
candidates.participation_mechanism: Apply the five-field audit to one current asset and mark the first decision your team cannot reconstruct without a meeting.
candidates.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
candidates.falsifier: Stop this route when senior practitioners cannot identify a missing decision or refine a release question after applying the audit.

body: 0:00 VISUAL: A desk fills with five cards labeled Brief, Evidence, Edit, Approval, and Release; one card is visibly missing.
0:02 VO: The expensive part is not making the asset. It is discovering which decision disappeared between these cards.
0:06 PROOF: On-screen labels connect the approved product fact to its source brief, editorial inference, named reviewer, and still-open release condition.
0:12 ACTION: Pause on the five cards, compare them with your last campaign handoff, and mark the card your team cannot produce.
candidates.cta: Inspect the evidence sequence, then judge whether the design-partner cohort is worth a closer look.
candidates.participation_mechanism: Compare the five on-screen cards with one current brief and mark the missing card before the video ends.

candidates.falsifier: Stop this route when qualified operators cannot name the missing handoff or explain why the release card matters after watching.

candidates.campaign_platform: The Boring Part Is the Product
candidates.hook: We built the part of an AI GTM employee that makes autonomous demos look less impressive: the release boundary.
progression: Disclose the builder affiliation before describing the category problem.
Explain why asset generation is not the difficult governance decision.
Name the trade-off created by withholding automatic external release.
Invite operators to falsify the design with a concrete audit.
body: AFFILIATION: We built ProofLaunch Cortex-X, so treat this as an operator teardown from the product team rather than an independent recommendation.
WHAT FAILED: The usual autonomy demo ends when an asset appears. That skips the harder question: which approved fact, editorial inference, and human judgment authorize release?
MECHANISM: The product keeps approved evidence, generation, review, activation preparation, and learning inside one governed record while automatic external release remains disabled.
TRADE-OFF: This design preserves a named release owner, but it also refuses the instant publish moment that makes many agent demonstrations feel magical.
candidates.cta: Inspect the evidence boundary and challenge the design before considering the cohort.
candidates.participation_mechanism: Audit one recent brief by marking the approved fact, editorial inference, release owner, and unresolved condition; post only the missing label if useful.
candidates.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
candidates.falsifier: Stop this route when practitioners cannot find a consequential release ambiguity or show that the governed record adds no decision value.

candidates.hook: Before you hire an AI GTM employee, audit the decision it is not allowed to make.
progression: Open with the release decision most autonomy demos omit.
Compare output speed with inspectable decision ownership and evidence.
Walk through the proof boundary and its unresolved conditions.
End with a buyer rule that rejects unsuitable autonomy.
body: TITLE: Before You Hire an AI GTM Employee, Audit This Release Decision
THUMBNAIL: One polished campaign asset sits beside a red card reading WHO AUTHORIZED RELEASE; the unanswered card dominates the frame.
0:00-0:30: This film does not ask whether AI can make content. It audits whether a buyer can reconstruct the evidence, inference, owner, and open condition before release.
CHAPTER: The Missing Decision; The Five-Field Record; Where Autonomy Stops; A Buyer Rejection Rule; The Human Release Boundary.
RECOMMENDATION BOUNDARY: Reject this approach if your team wants unsupervised publishing; inspect it only when decision provenance matters more than an instant autonomy demo.
candidates.cta: Inspect the evidence chapter, then decide whether the design-partner cohort deserves evaluation.
candidates.participation_mechanism: Audit the title-card question against one current process and score whether a named person can reconstruct the release decision without oral context.
candidates.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
candidates.falsifier: Stop this route when qualified buyers cannot distinguish the release-boundary problem from another generic claim about AI content production.

candidates.hook: The missing card in your campaign stack is usually the decision everyone assumed somebody else recorded.
progression: Create recognition with one visibly incomplete five-card system.
Name the function of each card without product decoration.
Place the bounded product fact on the evidence card.
Turn the carousel into a reusable release ritual.
body: SLIDE 1: Five cards should exist before release. Most campaign stacks can produce the asset card and cannot produce the decision card.
SLIDE 2: BRIEF names the audience and job. EVIDENCE names the approved fact. INFERENCE names the creative judgment introduced during production.
SLIDE 3: OWNER names the person accepting the remaining uncertainty. RELEASE states the explicit human decision; no card inherits authority from another.
SLIDE 4: Cortex-X keeps approved evidence, generation, review, activation preparation, and learning in a governed record without automatic external release.
SLIDE 5: Save the five labels, apply them to one current asset, and mark the first card that requires a meeting to reconstruct.
candidates.cta: Inspect the five-card evidence trail before considering the design-partner cohort.
candidates.participation_mechanism: Apply the five labels to one current carousel or video and mark the first missing card directly in your review notes.
candidates.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
candidates.falsifier: Stop this route when practitioners cannot use the five cards without additional explanation or cannot identify a consequential missing decision.

candidates.campaign_platform: Trust the Trail, Not the Asset
candidates.hook: A polished asset is evidence of production, not evidence of a justified GTM decision.
progression: Compress the category error into one falsifiable opening thesis.
Separate asset quality from the provenance of its decisions.
State the strongest counterargument without weakening the boundary.
Offer a dated adjudication rule for future evidence.
body: 1/ A polished asset proves that production happened. It does not prove that the audience assumption, approved fact, or release owner survived the production chain.
2/ The more useful trust object is a trail: source brief, approved evidence, editorial inference, named reviewer, unresolved condition, and explicit release state.
3/ Counterargument: a trail can become governance theater. Correct. If nobody changes a decision after reading it, the record is ceremony rather than control.
4/ Adjudication: inspect one current asset today, record the missing field, and revisit the same decision after new evidence enters the review.
candidates.cta: Inspect the decision trail; join the cohort only if the missing field changes your review.
candidates.participation_mechanism: Audit one current asset with the six-field trail and mark the first field that cannot survive a skeptical reply.
candidates.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
candidates.falsifier: Stop this route when informed readers cannot distinguish decision provenance from process theater or cannot name a changed review question.

candidates.hook: Evaluate an AI GTM agent by the release decision it exposes, not the number of assets it produces.
progression: Answer the buyer question before naming the product route.
Define decision criteria that reject unsafe or unsuitable autonomy.
Separate the approved fact from every unobserved outcome claim.
Give the buyer a no-signup evaluation action.
body: DIRECT ANSWER: A trustworthy evaluation asks whether the agent exposes its source brief, approved fact, editorial inference, release owner, unresolved condition, and external-action state before publication.
DECISION CRITERIA: Require inspectable evidence lineage, explicit human release authority, a bounded repair record, no invented outcome, and a stop condition tied to the buyer’s actual risk.
WHEN NOT TO USE: Reject this design when your operating model requires unsupervised publishing, undisclosed identity simulation, or decisions that no named person will own.
EVIDENCE BOUNDARY: ProofLaunch Cortex-X is a governed multimodal GTM employee that keeps automatic external release disabled; production effect and named-product superiority remain unobserved.
NEXT STEP: Apply the six criteria to one current vendor demonstration, then inspect the ProofLaunch evidence pack only if a missing decision becomes material.
candidates.cta: Inspect the evidence boundary after applying the publish-permission test to one current option.
candidates.participation_mechanism: Score one current AI GTM option against the six criteria and mark every answer that depends on a salesperson’s verbal assurance.
candidates.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
candidates.falsifier: Stop this route when buyers cannot use the criteria to reject an unsuitable option or identify an unresolved release decision.

candidates.hook: An AI GTM agent and an automation workflow differ most at the point where judgment becomes external action.
progression: Clarify the entities before comparing features or category labels.
Map evidence, inference, decision ownership, and external action separately.
Name the exception that invalidates a simple autonomy spectrum.
Route the unresolved boundary to a named owner.
body: ENTITY MAP: Brief supplies intent; approved evidence supplies factual bounds; model supplies a draft; reviewer owns judgment; release state controls external action.
COMPARISON CRITERIA: Compare systems by evidence lineage, inference disclosure, repair history, named decision rights, permission scope, and the ability to deny release cleanly.
EXCEPTION: A highly autonomous internal draft can remain safer than a simple automation when only the automation holds unsupervised external-action authority.
SOURCE BOUNDARY: The approved product fact supports asset preparation only; it does not support observed reach, preference, conversion, revenue, or competitor-superiority conclusions.
OWNER ACTION: Mark the first boundary your current system cannot explain, then route that unresolved decision to the person accountable for release.
candidates.cta: Inspect the evidence map after comparing one real decision boundary from your current stack.
candidates.participation_mechanism: Compare one agent and one automation with the six criteria, then mark the first external action that lacks a named human owner.
candidates.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
candidates.falsifier: Stop this route when the entity map does not change a buyer question or cannot separate internal autonomy from external authority.

candidates.hook: A useful answer about AI GTM employees should expose what the evidence cannot yet justify.
progression: State the research question in a form a buyer can audit.
Answer directly with a six-part evidence requirement.
Explain the method without implying a hidden benchmark result.
End with limitations and a stable update boundary.
body: QUESTION: What evidence should a buyer require before trusting an AI GTM employee with a campaign release decision?
DIRECT ANSWER: Require the source brief, approved fact, editorial inference, named reviewer, unresolved condition, and explicit external-action state in one inspectable record.
METHOD: Evaluate a frozen brief through generation and review, bind every artifact to its evidence boundary, and preserve denial as a valid human outcome.
LIMITATION: This method evaluates decision provenance and release control; it does not establish human preference, organic breakout, conversion, revenue, or superiority over named products.
UPDATED: 2026-08-03 — no production effect observed.

candidates.hook: The popular autonomy ladder breaks when a less autonomous system holds more external authority.
progression: Lead with the counterexample that invalidates a simple autonomy score.
Separate internal reasoning freedom from permission to act externally.
Define the conditions that change the safer recommendation.
Give decision makers a reversible comparison framework.
body: COMMON MODEL: Buyers often rank agent systems on a single ladder from assistant to autonomous employee, assuming that more autonomous reasoning necessarily creates more operational risk.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: A model may reason freely inside a bounded draft node while a deterministic release gate denies every external action; a simple automation may publish immediately.
BOUNDARY CONDITIONS: The comparison changes with permission scope, evidence sensitivity, reversibility, named ownership, denial behavior, and whether the action reaches a customer or budget.
DECISION FRAMEWORK: Score internal autonomy and external authority separately, then inspect evidence lineage, repair history, unresolved conditions, and the human decision required for release.
UPDATED: 2026-08-03 — no production effect observed.

candidates.hook: Multimodal proof becomes useful only when every visual state preserves the same claim boundary.
progression: Name the entity without borrowing a result from its media.
Bind text evidence to the exact approved product fact.
Design media states that expose rather than decorate provenance.
Show which human decision the relationship leaves unresolved.
body: ENTITY: ProofLaunch Cortex-X is presented as the governed product under evaluation; no customer, competitor, or performance result enters the entity record.
TEXT EVIDENCE: The source brief, approved product fact, editorial inference, named reviewer, and release state remain separate, readable evidence objects.
MEDIA EVIDENCE: Five rights-clear cards depict Brief, Evidence, Inference, Owner, and Release; each card carries a visible provenance label and no simulated result.
RELATIONSHIP: The media sequence mirrors the text record, so a summarized answer cannot turn a preparation fact into a publication or outcome claim.
LIMITATION: The proof graph demonstrates cross-modal consistency for this fixture only; broader accuracy, human preference, and production effect remain unobserved.

candidates.falsifier: Stop this route when reviewers cannot detect a text-media contradiction or cannot identify the human decision left unresolved by the graph.

candidates.hook: Before launch, a governed GTM employee can prove process facts; it cannot prove market response.
progression: Pose the narrow research question that keeps outcome claims separate.
Map owned evidence separately from external or missing sources.
State the finding and strongest disagreement as distinct blocks.
Translate the evidence gap into a bounded buyer decision.
body: RESEARCH QUESTION: Which claims about an AI GTM employee are justified before any external publication, audience response, conversion event, or recognized revenue exists?
SOURCE MAP: Owned evidence may establish the frozen brief, approved fact, generated draft, review record, permission state, and human release decision; market evidence remains absent.
FINDING: The defensible pre-launch claim concerns preparation and provenance. Preference, reach, conversion, revenue, and named-product superiority require separate observed evidence.
DISAGREEMENT: Some teams treat a polished artifact or green regression suite as market proof; those artifacts verify production behavior, not an audience response.
DECISION IMPLICATION: Inspect the preparation ledger for operational fit, but withhold market-effect and superiority judgments until authorized baselines and real observations exist.
UPDATED: 2026-08-03 — no production effect observed.

candidates.hook: The fastest decision packet is unsafe when nobody can deny the external action cleanly.
progression: Declare the public and authorized-context boundary before joining evidence.
List decision options without letting the artifact choose among them.
Assign the unresolved action to a named human role.
Preserve the denial and audit handoff as first-class outcomes.
body: PERMISSION BOUNDARY: This public launch draft contains no tenant context and grants no authority to publish, send, spend, mutate strategy, or cross an access boundary.
AUTHORIZED EVIDENCE: Only the frozen brief, approved product fact, generated artifact, deterministic checks, and explicit human decisions may enter this packet.
DECISION OPTIONS: Approve for a named next review, return with a bounded repair instruction, deny release, or request specific evidence without triggering an external action.
OWNER ACTION: A named GTM release owner chooses one option, records the unresolved condition, and retains responsibility for every permission change.
AUDIT HANDOFF: The packet carries source identifiers, artifact digest, review state, denied actions, and the exact evidence required for the next decision.

candidates.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
candidates.falsifier: Stop this route when reviewers cannot deny an external action cleanly or cannot reconstruct which evidence authorized the current decision state.
